title: A gate's host_unchecked reason can be set with backlog.py, and the host word check skips 'host-bound' wording
goal: Found at the SP-d3hybrlv start: ST-pjkmiyqe gate g1 asked who reshapes a story on a host-bound sprint, and start warned that it names a host setup with no --host-check; no backlog.py command sets a gate's host_unchecked reason (only gate add --host-check exists), so the warning could not be answered. backlog.py sets host_unchecked on an existing gate, and the host-word check does not fire on a gate that names no setup.
notes: Merged from ST-sz525jlz “start's host-setup warning tells a url's host from a host setup, and set can record host_unchecked on a gate” at the 2026-10-10 backlog triage: Near-duplicate of the older ST-7avb5uo6 (set a gate's host_unchecked with backlog.py, host-word check skips non-setup wording); bl_plan.py:238 HOST_WORDS still matches any 'host'. Must absorb: 'host' in a url sense does not fire the start warning. Its goal: bl_plan's HOST_WORDS warning at start no longer fires on 'host' used as a url's host (a routes-table or web host), and backlog.py set or gate gives a way to record a gate's host_unchecked reason on an existing gate, so a start warning can be acted on. Answers SP-evkj4avq, where start warned of ST-5zpbfax2 gate g1 for the word host in a url sense, and no command could record the reason (a note was refused as longer than TEXT_MAX). Its checks: {"run": ["python3", "_tools/backlog.py", "check"]} Its touches: _tools/bl_plan.py, _tools/bl_items.py, kb/_self/backlog.md
